requirements.title: Registering a workspace
requirements.rationale: A workspace that cannot follow origin or whose main branch is already unhealthy would fail every item nightshift drives in it.

criteria.condition: an authenticated client requests `POST /api/v1/workspaces` with `{"slug", "health_command", "health_timeout"?, "daily_tokens"?, "adopt_policy"?}` and all five registration checks pass
criteria.action: run the checks in the order owner, `sync_enabled`, sync, policy, health command, each with the worker token, then store the workspace with the state `green`
criteria.contract: status 201 with body `{"slug", "state": "green", "health_command", "health_timeout", "daily_tokens", "tokens_used_today": 0, "created_at", "policy_revision": null, "warning": string or null}`; `health_timeout` is the duration as Go prints it (`30m0s`); the hub saw, in this order, one `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}`, one `POST …/sync`, one `GET …/policy` and one fetch over `/git/`; the health command ran once, in a clone at the `local_sha` the sync reported for the default branch

setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) holding the workspace `demo`, owned by the worker token's user, with a git repository of one commit, `sync_enabled` on, a sync result `up_to_date` and a policy whose `default` requires the three checks with `fresh_checks`
a workspace service over a store copied from the template and a clones directory in a temporary directory
check.pseudocode: new file internal/workspace/register_test.go, through the router: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces', {slug: 'demo', health_command: 'test -f README.md && git rev-parse HEAD > "$OUT"'}); assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.state == 'green'; assert r.json.policy_revision == null; assert the fake hub's request log is [GET workspace, POST sync, GET policy, git fetch]; assert the file $OUT holds the sync's local_sha; assert service.Get('demo') returns the stored workspace

criteria.condition: the hub answers the read of the workspace with `404`, or the workspace object's `access` is not `owner`
criteria.action: refuse the registration without running a later check
criteria.contract: status 409 with body `{"error_type": "conflict", "message"}` where `message` is `workspace not found` for the 404 and `not the owner of <slug>` otherwise; no workspace is stored; the hub saw no sync request

setup: the fake hub and service of the registration test above; each row changes one thing on the fake hub
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go, one table for every way a registration is refused before the health command; these rows: {no such workspace -> 'workspace not found', access 'member' -> 'not the owner of demo', access 'admin' -> 'not the owner of demo'}: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces', body); assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error_type == 'conflict'; assert r.json.message == want; assert service.List() is empty; assert the fake hub saw no request after the one that decided the row

criteria.condition: the workspace's setting `sync_enabled` is `false`, or the sync is answered with an error, or it reports the default branch with a result other than `up_to_date`, `fast_forward` or `created`, or does not report it
criteria.action: refuse the registration without running a later check
criteria.contract: status 409 `conflict` with `message`: `sync is disabled for <slug>` (and no sync request sent); `default branch is ahead of origin` for `ahead`; `default branch has diverged from origin` for `diverged`; `default branch: sync reported <result>` for another result; `default branch <name> is not on origin` for a missing entry; `hub answered <status> <error_type>: <message>` for an error of the hub; no workspace is stored and no policy request is sent

criteria.condition: the health command exits with a code other than 0, or has not ended when the health timeout has passed, or cannot be started, or the workspace cannot be cloned at the tip of its default branch
criteria.action: refuse the registration, ending the command and every process it started when it timed out
criteria.contract: status 409 `conflict` with `message` `health command exited <N>`, `health command timed out`, `health command could not be started: <error>` or `cannot clone <slug>: <error>`, and for the first two the member `output`, a list of the last 50 lines the command wrote to standard output and standard error; no workspace is stored; no `PUT …/policy` is sent, also with `adopt_policy: true`

setup: the fake hub and service of the registration test above
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go, a table over {health_command 'seq 1 60; exit 3' -> 'health command exited 3' and output == lines 11..60, health_command 'echo started; sleep 60' with health_timeout '100ms' -> 'health command timed out' and output == ['started'] and the answer arrives within 5s, the fake hub's git endpoint answering 500 -> message starts with 'cannot clone demo: '}, each also with adopt_policy true against a policy that lacks the checks: assert r.status == 409; assert service.List() is empty; assert the fake hub saw no PUT of the policy

criteria.condition: the body of `POST /api/v1/workspaces` is not a JSON object, or has an empty `slug` or an empty `health_command`, or a `health_timeout` that is not a Go duration greater than zero, or a `daily_tokens` that is not an integer of 1 or more
criteria.action: reject the request without asking the hub
criteria.contract: status 400 with body `{"error_type": "invalid_request", "message"}` naming the member; no workspace is stored; the hub saw no request

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go, through the router, a table over the bodies {'[]', slug '', no health_command, health_timeout 'soon', health_timeout '0s', health_timeout '-1m', daily_tokens 0, daily_tokens -5, daily_tokens 'many'}: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces', body); assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert the fake hub's request count == 0

criteria.condition: a registration names a slug that is registered already, or one whose registration is still running
criteria.action: refuse the registration without asking the hub and leave the stored workspace unchanged
criteria.contract: status 409 `conflict` with `message` `<slug> is registered already` or `registration of <slug> is in progress`; of two registrations of one slug sent at once exactly one is answered 201

setup: the fake hub and service of the registration test above; a health command that waits for a file the test creates
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go: start post(demo) in a goroutine; once the health command runs, r2 = post(demo); assert r2.status == 409 and r2.json.message == 'registration of demo is in progress'; create the file; assert the first answer is 201; r3 = post(demo with another health_command); assert r3.status == 409 and r3.json.message == 'demo is registered already'; assert service.Get('demo').HealthCommand is the first one

criteria.action: for any registration that omits `health_timeout` or `daily_tokens`, store 30 minutes and the service's `DefaultDailyTokens` (50,000,000 unless another package set it) respectively, as they are at the time of the registration

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go, a table over {both omitted -> '30m0s' and 50000000, DefaultDailyTokens set to 7 before -> 7, health_timeout '90s' and daily_tokens 12 -> '1m30s' and 12}: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces', body); assert r.json.health_timeout and r.json.daily_tokens; set DefaultDailyTokens to 9 afterwards; assert service.Get(slug).DailyTokens is unchanged

criteria.condition: a route of this package that asks the hub (registration, show, protect, unprotect) is requested while the hub client reports the worker credential as not available, or a request to the hub fails with a connection error or a timeout
criteria.action: answer without storing or writing anything
criteria.contract: status 503 with body `{"error_type": "hub_unavailable", "message"}`; no workspace is stored and no rule is recorded

setup: the service over a hub client whose fake hub was stopped, with one workspace inserted directly into the store
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go, a table over {POST /api/v1/workspaces, GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo, POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/policy/rules, DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/demo/policy/rules/x}: assert r.status == 503; assert r.json.error_type == 'hub_unavailable'; and GET /api/v1/workspaces answers 200 with demo

requirements.title: The policy's three checks and its sensitive rules
requirements.rationale: A change lands without the person only because the hub refuses it until nightshift's own checks passed on exactly that version.

criteria.action: for any policy document, name as lacking the checks the `default` requirement and every rule whose requirement has `block` false, where the requirement's `checks` do not hold all of `nightshift-gate`, `nightshift-review` and `nightshift-release` or its `fresh_checks` is false, in the order `default` first and then the rules in document order, and never a rule whose requirement blocks
criteria.contract: `policy.Missing(document)` returns the names, `default` for the default requirement; an empty list means the policy requires the three checks

check.pseudocode: new file internal/policy/policy_test.go, a table over documents {revision 0 with no rules -> ['default'], default complete and no rules -> [], default complete and a rule with two of the three -> [that rule], a rule with all three and fresh_checks false -> [that rule], a blocking rule with no checks -> not named, default and two rules lacking -> ['default', rule1, rule2] in document order, a rule naming the three among other checks with fresh_checks true -> not named}: assert policy.Missing(doc) == want

criteria.condition: a registration without `adopt_policy` finds that the workspace's policy lacks the three checks in `default` or in a rule that does not block
criteria.action: refuse the registration without running the health command and without writing the policy
criteria.contract: status 409 `conflict` with `message` `policy of <slug> does not require nightshift's checks in: <names joined by ", ">; run again with --adopt-policy`; no workspace is stored; the hub saw no `PUT …/policy` and no fetch over `/git/`

setup: the fake hub and service of the registration test, with a policy whose `default` is empty and which has the rules `docs` (no checks) and `secrets` (block)
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces', {slug: 'demo', health_command: 'true'}); assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.message == "policy of demo does not require nightshift's checks in: default, docs; run again with --adopt-policy"; assert the fake hub's policy revision is unchanged; assert no git fetch was seen; assert service.List() is empty

criteria.condition: a registration with `adopt_policy: true` finds the policy lacking the three checks and the health command has exited 0
criteria.action: append the missing ones of `nightshift-gate`, `nightshift-review` and `nightshift-release`, in that order, to the `checks` of every requirement named as lacking and set its `fresh_checks` to true, changing no other member and no blocking rule, write the document with `PUT …/policy` and `If-Match` set to the revision it read, and then store the workspace
criteria.contract: status 201 whose `policy_revision` is the revision the hub answered; the hub's policy afterwards passes the check of REQ-2.1, keeps every rule in its place with its `paths`, `exclude`, `targets`, `approvals`, `approvers` and the checks it had; a registration with `adopt_policy: true` of a policy that lacks nothing sends no `PUT` and answers `policy_revision: null`

setup: the fake hub with the policy of the refusal test above, at revision 2, the rule `docs` naming the check `spell`
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces', {slug: 'demo', health_command: 'true', adopt_policy: true}); assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.policy_revision == 3; p = fakeHub.Policy('demo'); assert p.default.checks == the three and p.default.fresh_checks; assert p.rules[docs].checks == ['spell', the three]; assert p.rules[secrets] is unchanged; assert the PUT carried If-Match 2; assert policy.Missing(p) is empty. Second case, a complete policy with adopt_policy true: assert no PUT and policy_revision == null. The pure step in internal/policy/policy_test.go: assert policy.Missing(policy.Adopt(doc)) is empty for every document of the table above

criteria.condition: the hub answers the adopting `PUT …/policy` with `412 revision_mismatch`
criteria.action: refuse the registration and store nothing
criteria.contract: status 409 `conflict` with `message` `policy changed meanwhile; run the command again`; no workspace is stored; the write is not sent a second time

setup: the fake hub replaces the policy of `demo` while the health command runs
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go: the health command signals the test, which calls fakeHub.ReplacePolicy; assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.message == 'policy changed meanwhile; run the command again'; assert the fake hub saw exactly one PUT; assert service.List() is empty

criteria.action: for any policy document, treat as sensitive the `default` requirement and every rule whose requirement has `approvals` of 1 or more or `block` true, and no other
criteria.contract: `policy.Sensitive(document)` returns them in the order `rules` first in document order, then `default`, each with its name (`default` for the default requirement), its `paths`, its `approvals` and its `block`

check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/policy_test.go, a table over documents {no rules and an empty default -> [], a rule with approvals 1 -> [it], a rule with block -> [it], a rule with checks only -> [], default with approvals 2 -> [default with no paths], a mix -> the rules in document order then default}: assert policy.Sensitive(doc) == want

criteria.condition: a registration succeeds and the policy, as it is after an adoption, has no sensitive rule
criteria.action: answer the registration with the warning `no path of <slug> is marked sensitive; every change lands without you`
criteria.contract: the 201 body's `warning` is that line; it is `null` when a rule or `default` requires an approval or blocks

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/register_test.go, a table over policies {complete default only -> warning == 'no path of demo is marked sensitive; every change lands without you', plus a blocking rule -> null, plus a rule with approvals 1 and the three checks -> null}: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces', body); assert r.json.warning == want

requirements.title: Marking and unmarking sensitive paths
requirements.rationale: The person says where they are needed in the one place the hub enforces it, without writing policy JSON by hand.

criteria.condition: an authenticated client requests `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/policy/rules` with `{"globs": [string, …], "block"?: false, "name"?}` for a registered workspace
criteria.action: read the policy, insert before every other rule one rule with the globs as `paths` and the requirement `{"approvals": 1, "approvers": ["owner"], "checks": ["nightshift-gate", "nightshift-review", "nightshift-release"], "fresh_checks": true}`, write the document with `If-Match` set to the revision it read, and record the rule's name for that workspace in its store
criteria.contract: status 201 with body `{"rule": {"name", "paths", "require"}, "revision": <the revision the hub answered>}`; the hub's policy holds the rule at index 0 and every earlier rule after it, unchanged and in the same order

setup: a fake hub whose workspace `demo` has a policy at revision 3 with the rule `docs`
a service with `demo` inserted directly into its store
check.pseudocode: new file internal/workspace/protect_test.go, through the router: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/policy/rules', {globs: ['deploy/**', 'ops/*.yaml']}); assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.revision == 4; assert r.json.rule.name == 'nightshift-1'; p = fakeHub.Policy('demo'); assert p.rules[0] == {name: 'nightshift-1', paths: both globs, require: approvals 1, approvers ['owner'], the three checks, fresh_checks true, block false}; assert p.rules[1].name == 'docs'; assert the PUT carried If-Match 3

criteria.condition: the request to protect carries `"block": true`
criteria.action: write the rule with the requirement `{"block": true}` in place of the approval and the checks
criteria.contract: the hub's rule at index 0 has `block` true, `approvals` 0 and no checks; the answer's `rule.require.block` is true

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/protect_test.go: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/policy/rules', {globs: ['deploy/secrets/**'], block: true}); assert r.status == 201; assert fakeHub.Policy('demo').rules[0].require == {approvals: 0, approvers: ['owner'], checks: [], fresh_checks: false, block: true}

criteria.action: for any rule it writes, use the `name` the request gives, and without one the name `nightshift-<n>` where n is one greater than the highest number among the policy's rules named `nightshift-<number>`, and 1 when there is none

check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/policy_test.go, a table over the rule names a document holds {none -> 'nightshift-1', ['nightshift-1'] -> 'nightshift-2', ['nightshift-1', 'nightshift-7', 'docs'] -> 'nightshift-8', ['nightshift-x', 'nightshift-02'] -> 'nightshift-3'}: assert policy.NextName(doc) == want. In internal/workspace/protect_test.go: post with name 'deploy' writes a rule named 'deploy'

criteria.condition: a glob of the request is empty, longer than 255 characters or starts with `/`, or the list of globs is empty, or the hub answers the write with `400 invalid_policy` whose `details.field` begins with `paths`
criteria.action: refuse the protection, sending no write to the hub for a glob it refused itself
criteria.contract: status 400 with body `{"error_type": "invalid_glob", "message": "glob \"<glob>\" is refused: <reason>"}`, the hub's message as the reason where the hub refused; the hub's policy is unchanged and no rule is recorded

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/protect_test.go, a table over globs {[''], ['/etc/**'], [256 characters], [] -> 400 invalid_glob and the fake hub saw no PUT; ['a[b'] which the fake hub is scripted to refuse with invalid_policy details.field 'paths[0]' -> 400 invalid_glob}: assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error_type == 'invalid_glob'; assert the fake hub's policy revision is unchanged; assert a later unprotect of the name answers 'not a rule nightshift wrote'

criteria.condition: the hub answers the write of a protection or of an unprotection with `412 revision_mismatch`
criteria.action: refuse the request without sending the write again and leave its record of rules unchanged
criteria.contract: status 409 with body `{"error_type": "conflict", "message": "policy changed meanwhile; run the command again"}`; the hub saw exactly one `PUT`

setup: the fake hub replaces the policy between the service's read and its write, through a hook on its GET
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/protect_test.go, a table over {protect, unprotect of a recorded rule}: assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.message == 'policy changed meanwhile; run the command again'; assert the fake hub saw one PUT; for protect assert the name is not recorded, for unprotect assert it still is

criteria.condition: an authenticated client requests `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/policy/rules/{name}` for a rule that the store records as written by a protection of that workspace
criteria.action: read the policy, write it without that rule with `If-Match` set to the revision it read, and forget the record; where the policy no longer holds the rule, forget the record and write nothing
criteria.contract: status 200 with body `{"revision": <the policy's revision after the request>}`; every other rule is unchanged and in the same order; a second request for the same name is answered as for a rule nightshift did not write

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/protect_test.go: protect ['deploy/**'] -> nightshift-1 at revision 4; r = delete('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/policy/rules/nightshift-1'); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.revision == 5; assert fakeHub.Policy('demo').rules names == ['docs']; assert a second delete answers 409. Second case: protect, then the fake hub drops the rule by itself; delete answers 200 with the hub's current revision and the fake hub saw no further PUT

criteria.condition: a request to unprotect names a rule that the store does not record as written by a protection of that workspace
criteria.action: refuse it without asking the hub
criteria.contract: status 409 with body `{"error_type": "conflict", "message": "not a rule nightshift wrote"}`; the hub's policy is unchanged, also when it holds a rule of that name

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/protect_test.go, a table over names {'docs' (in the policy, written by the person), 'nope' (nowhere), a rule protect wrote for another workspace, a rule protect wrote for demo before demo was removed and inserted again}: r = delete(route); assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.message == 'not a rule nightshift wrote'; assert the fake hub saw no PUT

criteria.condition: a request to protect gives a `name` that a rule of the policy carries already, or one that is `default`, longer than 63 characters or holds a character other than a lower-case letter, a digit, `_` or `-`
criteria.action: refuse the protection without writing the policy
criteria.contract: status 409 `conflict` with `message` `rule <name> exists already` for a taken name; status 400 `invalid_request` for a name outside the format; the hub saw no `PUT` and no rule is recorded

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/protect_test.go, a table over names {'docs' -> 409 'rule docs exists already', 'default' -> 400, 'Deploy' -> 400, 64 characters -> 400, 'a b' -> 400}: r = post(route, {globs: ['x/**'], name}); assert r.status and r.json.error_type; assert the fake hub saw no PUT

requirements.title: Settings, state and removal
requirements.rationale: The person has to see what nightshift believes about a workspace and be able to change what they told it.

criteria.condition: an authenticated client requests `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` for a registered workspace
criteria.action: answer the workspace object with the sensitive rules of the policy as the hub holds it at that moment
criteria.contract: status 200 with the workspace object plus `sensitive_rules`, a list of `{"name", "paths", "approvals", "block"}` in the order of REQ-2.5, empty when there is none

setup: a fake hub whose policy of `demo` has the rules `nightshift-1` (approvals 1, paths deploy/**), `docs` (checks only) and `secrets` (block)
a service with `demo` inserted directly into its store
check.pseudocode: new file internal/workspace/workspace_test.go, through the router: r = get('/api/v1/workspaces/demo'); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.slug == 'demo' and r.json.state == 'green'; assert r.json.sensitive_rules == [{name: 'nightshift-1', paths: ['deploy/**'], approvals: 1, block: false}, {name: 'secrets', paths: [...], approvals: 0, block: true}]; after fakeHub.ReplacePolicy(empty): assert the next GET has sensitive_rules == []

criteria.condition: an authenticated client requests `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` with one or more of `health_command`, `health_timeout` and `daily_tokens`
criteria.action: store the given values, leave the others, run no check and ask the hub nothing, so that the next run of the health command and the next read of the limit use them
criteria.contract: status 200 with the workspace object carrying the new values; `service.Get(slug)` returns them; the hub saw no request

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/workspace_test.go, a table over bodies {health_command only, health_timeout '45s' only, daily_tokens 9 only, all three}: r = patch('/api/v1/workspaces/demo', body); assert r.status == 200; assert the given members changed and the others did not, in r.json and in service.Get('demo'); assert the fake hub's request count == 0

criteria.condition: the body of a `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` names none of the three members, an unknown member, an empty `health_command`, a `health_timeout` that is not a Go duration greater than zero, or a `daily_tokens` that is not an integer of 1 or more
criteria.action: reject the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: status 400 with body `{"error_type": "invalid_request", "message"}`; the stored workspace is as before

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/workspace_test.go, a table over bodies {'{}', {state: 'red'}, {health_command: ''}, {health_timeout: '0s'}, {daily_tokens: 0}, {daily_tokens: 1.5}}: r = patch(route, body); assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert service.Get('demo') equals the workspace before

criteria.condition: an authenticated client requests `GET /api/v1/workspaces` or `GET /api/v1/status`
criteria.action: report every registered workspace in the order of its slug, with `tokens_used_today` taken from the source registered with `SetTokensUsed` and 0 while none is registered, and with the members every function registered with `Decorate` adds to the workspace object
criteria.contract: `GET /api/v1/workspaces` answers 200 `{"workspaces": [<workspace object>, …]}`, an empty list when none is registered; the `workspaces` member of `GET /api/v1/status` is a list of `{"slug", "state", "tokens_used_today"}` in the same order; neither asks the hub

setup: an API server of package 01 with this package's routes and its `workspaces` status source registered; the workspaces `zeta` and `alpha` inserted directly into the store
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/workspace_test.go: r = get('/api/v1/workspaces'); assert slugs == ['alpha', 'zeta'] and every tokens_used_today == 0; service.SetTokensUsed(func(slug) -> 42 for 'zeta'); service.Decorate(func(slug, obj) { obj['paused'] = slug == 'alpha' }); r = get('/api/v1/workspaces'); assert zeta.tokens_used_today == 42 and alpha.paused == true; s = get('/api/v1/status'); assert s.json.workspaces == [{slug: 'alpha', state: 'green', tokens_used_today: 0}, {slug: 'zeta', state: 'green', tokens_used_today: 42}]; with an empty store assert both lists == []; assert the fake hub's request count == 0

criteria.condition: another package calls `SetState(ctx, slug, state)` with `green`, `red` or `held` for a registered workspace
criteria.action: store the state, so that every later read of the workspace reports it, also after a restart of nightshiftd
criteria.contract: the call returns no error; `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}`, the list and the status report the new `state`; a store closed and opened again reports it

setup: a service over a store file in a temporary directory
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/workspace_test.go, a table over {red, held, green after red}: service.SetState(ctx, 'demo', state); assert service.Get('demo').State == state; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces').json.workspaces[0].state == state; close the store, open it again with a new service; assert Get('demo').State == state and its settings are as stored

criteria.condition: `SetState` is called with a state other than `green`, `red` or `held`, or a route or function of this package names a slug that is not registered
criteria.action: return an error and change nothing
criteria.contract: `SetState` with an unknown state returns an error naming the state; a function given an unregistered slug returns `workspace.ErrNotFound`; `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` and both routes under `…/policy/rules` answer status 404 with body `{"error_type": "not_found", "message": "workspace <slug> is not registered"}` without asking the hub

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/workspace_test.go: assert service.SetState(ctx, 'demo', 'blue') != nil and Get('demo').State == 'green'; assert errors.Is(service.SetState(ctx, 'nope', 'red'), workspace.ErrNotFound); a table over {GET /api/v1/workspaces/nope, PATCH …/nope, DELETE …/nope, POST …/nope/policy/rules, DELETE …/nope/policy/rules/x}: assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.message == 'workspace nope is not registered'; assert the fake hub's request count == 0

criteria.condition: an authenticated client requests `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` for a registered workspace and every guard registered with `AddRemoveGuard` returns no error
criteria.action: remove the workspace's row, its recorded rule names and its clone directory, then call every function registered with `OnRemoved` with the slug, in the order they were registered, and send no request to the hub
criteria.contract: status 204; the list no longer holds the slug; the clone directory does not exist; each hook was called once; the fake hub saw no request and its policy still holds the rules protect wrote; the slug can be registered again

setup: a registered `demo` with a clone directory and one recorded rule; two `OnRemoved` hooks that append to a list
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/workspace_test.go: reset the fake hub's request log; r = delete('/api/v1/workspaces/demo'); assert r.status == 204; assert service.List() is empty; assert the clone directory is gone; assert hooks ran as ['first:demo', 'second:demo']; assert the fake hub's request count == 0; assert a new registration of demo answers 201

criteria.condition: a guard registered with `AddRemoveGuard` returns an error for the slug of a removal
criteria.action: refuse the removal with the first such guard's error, calling no later guard and no `OnRemoved` function
criteria.contract: status 409 with body `{"error_type": "conflict", "message": <the guard's error text>}`; the workspace, its recorded rules and its clone directory are as before

requirements.title: Running commands and cloning from the hub
requirements.rationale: The health command here, and the gate and the session clones of later packages, all run foreign code in a checkout; one implementation bounds its time, its output and the user it runs as.

criteria.condition: a caller runs a command line through `(*command.Runner).Run(ctx, command.Spec{Dir, Line, Timeout, TailLines, Env})`
criteria.action: run the line with `sh -c` in the directory, with the given variables added to the daemon's environment, wait for it, and keep the last `TailLines` lines of its standard output and standard error together, each line cut at 4,096 bytes
criteria.contract: returns `command.Result{ExitCode, TimedOut: false, Tail}` and a nil error for a command that ran, whatever its exit code; `Tail` holds at most `TailLines` lines in the order written, without line ends

check.pseudocode: new file internal/command/command_test.go, a table over {'echo out; echo err >&2; exit 0' -> code 0 and tail holds 'out' and 'err', 'exit 7' -> code 7 and an empty tail, 'seq 1 500' with TailLines 50 -> tail == lines 451..500, 'pwd' -> tail == [Dir], 'echo $FOO' with Env FOO=bar -> ['bar'], one line of 10,000 bytes -> one tail line of 4,096 bytes, 2 MB of output without a line end -> returns with one line of 4,096 bytes}: res, err = runner.Run(ctx, spec); assert err == nil; assert res

criteria.condition: a command has not ended when its `Timeout` has passed, or the context given to `Run` is cancelled
criteria.action: kill the command's process group, so that the processes it started end with it, and return what it had written
criteria.contract: returns `Result{TimedOut: true, Tail}` and a nil error for the timeout, and the context's error for a cancellation; `Run` returns within 5 seconds of the timeout; no process of the command's group is left running

Second case: cancel ctx after 50ms; assert errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) and the child is gone

criteria.condition: the directory of a command does not exist, the line is empty, `Timeout` or `TailLines` is not greater than zero, or the process cannot be started
criteria.action: return an error without starting a process, and never end the daemon's own process
criteria.contract: `Run` returns a zero `Result` and a non-nil error naming the cause

check.pseudocode: in internal/command/command_test.go, a table over {Dir naming no directory, Line '', Timeout 0, TailLines 0}: res, err = runner.Run(ctx, spec); assert err != nil; assert res == command.Result{}

criteria.condition: another package has given the runner an identity with `(*command.Runner).SetIdentity(command.Identity)`
criteria.action: apply the identity to every process `Run` starts from then on, before the process starts, and start no process when the identity returns an error
criteria.contract: the identity function is called once per `Run` with the `*exec.Cmd` about to start; its error is returned by `Run` with a zero `Result`; without an identity, processes run as the daemon's user

criteria.action: clone the repository from the URL over HTTP, authenticating with HTTP Basic and the token as the password, running git through the given runner, and check the commit out detached
criteria.contract: returns nil; `git rev-parse HEAD` in the directory prints the commit; the working tree holds exactly the commit's files; the token appears neither in an argument of a git process, nor in the URL of the remote `origin`, nor in a file under the directory

symbols.name: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}
symbols.signature: scope workspaces:read (satisfied by workspaces:write); 200 workspace object {slug, kind: repository|fork, default_branch, owner_id, org_id, org_slug, status, head_sha, origin_head_sha, settings: {sync_enabled: bool, …every setting with its effective value}, hub_url: string|null, access: owner|member|admin, …}; 404 not_found for a workspace that does not exist or that the caller cannot read

symbols.name: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/sync
symbols.signature: scope workspaces:write, write access; no body; query reset_to_origin default false; 200 workspace object plus branches: [{name, result: created|up_to_date|fast_forward|ahead|diverged|reset|name_conflict, local_sha, origin_sha}]; 400 fork_has_no_origin; 400 sync_disabled; 409 workspace_busy|workspace_not_ready|workspace_archived; 502 upstream_error; 500 internal

symbols.name: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/policy
symbols.signature: scope changes:read (satisfied by changes:write); 200 {revision: int, default: requirement, rules: [{name, paths: [glob], exclude: [glob], targets?: [glob], require: requirement}], updated_at, updated_by}; requirement = {approvals: 0..10, approvers: [owner|member|user:<username>], checks: [string], fresh_checks: bool, block: bool}, every member present; header ETag: "<revision>"; revision 0 for a workspace that never set a policy

symbols.name: PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/policy
symbols.signature: scope workspaces:write, owner only; body {default?, rules?}; header If-Match: <revision> or "<revision>"; 200 the policy of the new revision; 400 invalid_policy with error.details {rule, index, field}; 400 not_supported_on_fork; 412 revision_mismatch; 409 workspace_archived; a rule name is lower-case letters, digits, _ and -, at most 63 characters, unique, not default; a path glob is 1 to 255 characters, not starting with /, with *, ** and ? as wildcards; at most 200 rules and 65,536 bytes

symbols.name: git smart HTTP
symbols.import_path: <hub_url> = <external URL of the hub>/git/<org slug>/<workspace slug>.git
symbols.signature: GET …/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack and POST …/git-upload-pack; HTTP Basic, the credential as the password, any user name; a PAT needs git:read (included in git:write) and read access to the workspace; protocol versions 0 and 2
